key_insight: An independent certificate checker provides guaranteed error bounds for PDE solver outputs, including finite-element solutions and neural predictions, without trusting the solver.
engineering_relevance: Certificate-based verification can help automated engineering simulation pipelines distinguish physically accurate predictions from outputs that merely appear converged.
method: Return an admissible potential and an exactly charge-conserving current alongside each solution.
Use a small independent checker to bound error against a written physics specification.
Apply the same checker to conventional solvers, LLM-written code, and neural surrogates.
evidence_signal: On the cardiac ablation problem, certificates rejected or refuted all five convergent buggy solvers, certified one LLM-written solver to 0.1%, and gave reduced-basis neural predictions bounds at most 0.0021% wide within the training range.
watch_item: Bounds guarantee agreement with the stated model, not physical reality, and become informative only when outputs are energy-accurate on a sufficiently resolving grid.
paper_title: Verifying the Outputs of PDE Solvers: From Finite Elements to Neural Surrogates
